## What's new

ChronoTask used to be purely event-driven: at the start of a slot it calls a service, at the end another one. Three cases were left uncovered: **"leave it alone for a while"** (a manual change was overwritten by the next slot), **"go back to the schedule"** (ChronoTask couldn't tell what should be active *now*) and **restarts** (if Home Assistant was off at a start/end time, the event was lost). 1.7 covers all three, generically — it works with any service that targets entities, nothing is specific to `climate`, and the rule format does not change.

### ⏸ Hold, resume and resync
- **`chronotask.hold`** — pause one or more entities (`minutes`, `until`, or no expiry; `reason` is free text). Rules do not touch held entities: if a rule targets several, only the held ones are removed from the call. A new hold replaces the previous one, timed holds resume by themselves, and holds survive restarts.
- **`chronotask.resume`** — remove the hold and, unless `apply: false`, run the action of the **current state**: the last past event (start or end of a slot) among the enabled rules that target the entity. Overnight slots, explicit end days, slots without an end and the Sunday→Monday wrap are handled; on a tie the start wins, so back-to-back slots work. Returns `{entity_id: {applied: start|end|null, rule}}`.
- **`chronotask.resync`** — apply the current state to every entity that is not held (or to the ones given). Never called automatically: call it after Home Assistant starts or after enabling a group of rules.

### 📡 The expected state, for your automations
- New attribute **`entities`** on `sensor.<planner>_rules`: for every targeted entity `scheduled`, `rule`, `since`, `expected_service`, `expected_data`, `next_change`, `hold`, `hold_until`, `hold_reason`.
- It is updated **before** a rule calls its service, so an automation that compares the real state with the expected one never mistakes a starting slot for a manual change.
- Every action runs with a fresh context and fires the event **`chronotask_action`** (`planner_id`, `rule_id`, `title`, `part`, `entity_ids`, `context_id`).
- `rules` and `entities` are excluded from the recorder history, so the database doesn't grow.

### 🌡 Real-world use: Tado-style radiator valves
Tested on a real setup with thermostatic valves integrated via HomeKit, reproducing the Tado app behaviour entirely locally: a weekly schedule (25 single-day rules became 4 multi-slot ones); a **manual change** from the app, a voice assistant or the physical knob is detected by comparing the valve with `entities` and held for N minutes per room; an **open window** holds the valve and turns it off until it is closed; **away mode** and the **heating season** switch work the same way; at **startup** a resync puts everything back on schedule. All scenarios call a single "back to schedule" script built on `hold`/`resume`. The full example (script, Jinja macros and scenario table) is in the README, section *Hold, resume and resync*.

### Good to know
- Only rules that name an `entity_id` (in the data or in `target`) can be held; rules on areas/devices are not affected.
- A `resume` that finds the entity `unavailable`/`unknown` logs a warning and does not retry — hence the `resync` after startup. Holds that expired while Home Assistant was off are removed at startup without applying anything.
- Holds are not part of export/import.

Also in this release: a `tests/` folder (no Home Assistant needed) and new ideas in the README roadmap (hold badge in the card, `chronotask.boost`, optional built-in override detection, `resync_on_start`, seasons/profiles).
